thread:
support-bot: :warning: Alert: Ticket ZEN-482 — customer 'Zenith' reporting ~40% throughput drop on Dedicated cluster eu-west-2. Auto-collected metrics attached: https://console.redwood/inbox/zen-482

jess: FYI — Zenith opened a support ticket. They say embedding endpoint throughput collapsed around 09:12 UTC, p95 up from 120ms -> 420ms, tail CPU on their side is fine. They provided request_id=rz-9a3f and sample payload.

kevin: thanks. can you paste the sample payload + model name they hit? also which capacity (dedicated pool id)?

jess: sample payload included 8 short texts (avg 220 tokens total / request). model: redwood/opt-13b-8k-quant. pool: ded-eu2-zenith-1 (4 x A100).

maya: hmm 220 tokens per request but 8 requests in flight -> net len ~1760 tokens concurrent. if KV cache policy changed or batching got aggressive it could blow up latency. any recent rollouts to that pool?

kevin: there was a minor runtime rollout last night (release 2026-03-16, commit abc1234) that tweaked batching heuristics. rolling back to previous release would be my quick validation. can we repro in perf?

alan: I'll kick off a perf-run against ded-eu2-zenith-1 with the customer's payload. running a controlled rps profile from perf-cluster now. command: `./perf-runner --pool ded-eu2-zenith-1 --model redwood/opt-13b-8k-quant --concurrency 8 --payload sample.json --duration 5m`

sofia: when you have a run, grab KV cache hit rate + kv-cache-size histogram, and gpu_sm_util, gpu_mem_used, and scheduler queue length. Also check `inflight_batch_size` histogram — the rollout changed the max batch target.

alan: perf started 09:37 UTC. early results: baseline throughput 180 rps -> current 110 rps, p95 ~410ms. attaching log excerpt:

```
[09:39:12] req rz-9a3f queued batch_size=64
[09:39:12] dispatch -> worker-2 (seq_len_est=1760) actual_tokens=1728
[09:39:12] gpu0 kernel_time 312ms, gpu1 318ms
[09:39:13] kvcache: hits=0.12, misses=0.88
[09:39:13] scheduler queue_depth=22
```

kevin: kvcache hit rate 12% is suspicious given repeated prefixes. Could be a key eviction policy or memory pressure. Did the rollout change shard affinity or eviction TTL?

maya: release note abc1234 changed `max_batch_target` from 32 -> 64 for latency-sensitive workloads. That could push hot sequences into bigger batches and increase kernel tail time for long ctx. For 1760 tokens that's costly. Suggest we run a quick hotfix toggling back to 32 on that pool.

jess: I can coordinate the rollback with account team and get customer permission for a quick canary. They want us to test first.

sofia: before toggling, let's confirm memory/GPU pressure: alan, can you run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and `nvml_profiler` during the next 2 mins and paste outputs? Also fetch `kv_eviction_ops` from metrics.

alan: grabbing now. early nvml shows occasional mem spikes up to 96% on gpu0 and gpu1, and SM util sitting ~85% but long kernels push tail. kv_eviction_ops spiked around same time as throughput drop.

kevin: that aligns. Plan: 1) temporary pool config change to restore max_batch_target=32 (canary on 1 host), 2) run perf-runner again, 3) if throughput recovers, schedule full rollout rollback and postmortem. Who can apply the pool override?

maya: I can apply the override to ded-eu2-zenith-1-canary. doing it now (will patch via ops API).

jess: customer okayed canary. pls ping when done and we'll route small % of traffic.

maya: override deployed at 09:54 UTC. toggled `max_batch_target=32` on one host.

alan: rerunning perf-runner against the canary host. command: `./perf-runner --host ded-eu2-zenith-1-canary-01 --model redwood/opt-13b-8k-quant --concurrency 8 --duration 3m`

alan: results after canary run: throughput 168 rps, p95 130ms, kvcache hits 0.78, scheduler queue_depth avg=6. nvml shows mem stable ~68%. logs:

```
[09:58:32] req rz-9a3f queued batch_size=28
[09:58:32] dispatch -> worker-2 (seq_len_est=1760) actual_tokens=1728
[09:58:33] gpu0 kernel_time 98ms, gpu1 102ms
[09:58:33] kvcache: hits=0.78, misses=0.22
[09:58:33] scheduler queue_depth=5
```

kevin: nice — clear delta. rollback looks like the right mitigation. maya, can you schedule full rollback for the pool and open a rollback change with SRE runbook? tag it with INCIDENT=ZEN-482.

maya: creating change now. planning staged rollback across hosts over 20m with health checks. change id CHG-6612.

jess: told customer we'll run rollback and monitor for 30m, then re-evaluate. they're relieved.

sofia: postmortem items: define safer default for max_batch_target when median seq_len > 512, add unit perf test with long-ctx workloads, and add an alert for kv_eviction_ops correlating with throughput drops.

kevin: agree. I'll own the postmortem and CL to add the perf test. tagging folks: @maya for rollback ops, @alan for perf metrics ingestion, @sofia for regression test design.

jess: will update the ticket ZEN-482 with canary results and rollback change id. keeping this thread open for any regressions. :thumbsup:
